heading: Identifiable heads, normalization and neurons contribute to self-repair
definition: much of self-repair is carried by identifiable parts (backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, anti-erasure neurons).
summary: Independent studies support backup and copy-suppression heads as contributors to self-repair in GPT-2 small on indirect object identification. The combined share of named mechanisms remains unquantified, while evidence for LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure under ablation remains limited to the original group.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: R2 for backup and copy-suppression heads in GPT-2 small IOI (arXiv:2607.01940#r2, arXiv:2610.02173#R9); R0 for final-LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons under ablation (original: arXiv:2402.15390#R15, arXiv:2402.15390#R19). 1-10B: R0 for anti-erasure neurons under ablation in the original's Llama-7B (arXiv:2402.15390#R20). A different group identifies counterweight neurons under contrastive swaps in Llama, Gemma, Qwen and Mistral instruct models (arXiv:2610.02173#R1, arXiv:2610.02173#R2, arXiv:2610.02173#R3, arXiv:2610.02173#R4); whether these reproduce the original anti-erasure mechanism remains uncertain. Final-normalization gain contributes at most 4.5% of measured recruitment under the audited swap conditions (arXiv:2610.02173#R19). Toy, 10-100B and >100B: no evidence in counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.V5.verdicts.supports.studies = 7; versions.V5.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0; versions.V5.tested_with_controls = 5. Independent evidence supports named contributors in GPT-2 small IOI: backup contributions increase after primary removal (arXiv:2607.01940#r2), and dose swaps recruit identified backup and copy-suppression heads (arXiv:2610.02173#R9, arXiv:2610.02173#R10). arXiv:2310.04625 shares two authors with an original, so its evidence counts as R1, not independent R2; its copy-suppression heads explain 39% of measured repair (arXiv:2310.04625#r1). That single-mechanism share does not establish that the combined named mechanisms are insufficient. Backup freezing costs 0.57±0.09 of IOI margin, against a post-primary-removal margin of 2.290±0.110; this is a causal diagnostic, not a partition of total repair (arXiv:2607.01940#r4). The combined share remains unreported, leaving 'much of' unquantified. Under ablation, LayerNorm and anti-erasure evidence remains the original's (arXiv:2402.15390#R15, arXiv:2402.15390#R19, arXiv:2402.15390#R20). counts: versions.V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1; the checker identifies that study as arXiv:2310.04625.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent measurements of final-LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons under zero, mean or resample ablation could raise those parts from R0 (arXiv:2402.15390#R15, arXiv:2402.15390#R19, arXiv:2402.15390#R20). Other useful results are a combined contribution of the named mechanisms, quantified named-head repair shares on general text across families, and tests above 10B parameters (counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size). Matched interventions could clarify why L10H6 responds to primary removal but has no certified coupling under the core dose swap (arXiv:2607.01940#r3; arXiv:2610.02173#R17).

source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

original_result.setup: They resample-ablated attention heads on The Pile and measured LayerNorm and final-layer neuron contributions on selected tokens.
original_result.result: LayerNorm repaired around 30% of the ablated head's direct effect on average across many layers. In Llama-7B, the top repairing neuron repaired 10% of the head's direct effect in over 40% of instances selected from the top 2% by head direct effect.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Negative heads and backup heads carried downstream repair after Name Mover ablation.
GPT-2-small backup name movers increased their contributions after primary heads were removed.
Identifiable counterweights carried compensation, with copy-suppression head L10.h7 showing the strongest coupling.
Backup-head behavior recurred across ablation distributions, and further backup heads existed.
Authors attributed masked Name Mover effects in GPT-2 small to downstream backup heads.
Primary-head removal increased backup importance and reduced Negative Name Mover suppression.
Copy-suppression heads contributed to GPT-2 Small self-repair after upstream copying heads were ablated.
Copy suppression explained part of repair; the unembedding direction did not explain backup-head repair.
Documented backup heads carried only part of GPT-2-small IOI repair.
Some backup heads lacked measurable coupling; final LayerNorm gain explained little recruitment under swaps.
Copy suppression explained some, but not all, GPT-2 Small IOI self-repair.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: How much of self-repair the named mechanisms carry together, in any model. Only single-mechanism shares are reported. This includes the combined share in GPT-2 Small IOI after primary name-mover removal.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines: arXiv:2608.19338 (fraction not quantified; group-level only), arXiv:2610.04017 (share not examined), lw:hhhmcWkgLwPmBuhx7 (share not measured), arXiv:2607.01940 (LayerNorm share not quantified). No row has a combined-share measure. Checker correction for arXiv:2607.01940#r4: backup-freezing loss is a causal load-bearing diagnostic, not a partition of total repair, and therefore does not supply the missing combined share.

untested.what: Measurements by studies other than the original of final LayerNorm's share of restored output and anti-erasure-neuron contributions under zero, mean or resample ablation. LayerNorm control experiments have been performed, but do not supply these measurements.
untested.basis: Checker correction for arXiv:2607.01940, Appendix C.2.2: LayerNorm-denominator and full-normalization freezing are experimental controls; neither measures final LayerNorm's share of restored output or anti-erasure neurons. arXiv:2610.02173#R19 measures normalization under a contrastive swap, with the stated caveat that the result need not hold for deletion. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_family records family coverage, not mechanism-specific contribution measurements.

untested.what: Quantified causal shares of self-repair carried by backup or copy-suppression heads in models other than GPT-2 Small.
untested.basis: arXiv:2310.04625#r1 measures the copy-suppression repair share in GPT-2 Small IOI. The checker distinguishes this from cross-model copy-suppression and anti-induction scores, GPT-2 Medium QK analysis and IOI direct logit attribution, and weaker copy suppression in Pythia (Appendices A–B, Figures 9–11). Appendix Q reports qualitative ablation-induced repair in Stanford GPT-2 Small E. lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r4 identifies candidate Llama backup heads from attention patterns without measuring their causal contribution. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.patching.by_family includes other families, but arXiv:2610.02173#R1–R8 concern neurons rather than backup or copy-suppression heads.

untested.what: Named mechanisms in models above 10B parameters.

wording_issues.issue: The combined share carried by all named parts is not reported. In GPT-2 Small IOI, copy-suppression heads L10H7 and L11H10 explain 39% of measured repair; this alone does not establish a limit on their combined contribution with other named mechanisms (arXiv:2310.04625 r1). Freezing documented backups causes an IOI margin loss of 0.57±0.09 logits against a post-primary-removal margin of 2.290±0.110 logits; this diagnostic is not a partition of total repair (arXiv:2607.01940 r4). The original's approximately 30% is LayerNorm repair divided by clean head direct effect, clipped to 0–100% per token and averaged after high-direct-effect filtering, not a share of total repair (arXiv:2402.15390 R15). Under contrastive swaps in Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-it and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with 50 pairs per family, correct-sign final-norm contributions reach 4.5% of recruitment; the largest ×1 correction is 0.6% (arXiv:2610.02173 R19).

Part of the compensation comes from heads outside the documented sets: the contribution of heads other than the documented backups shifts from −0.77 to +0.39 (arXiv:2607.01940 verdict reason). This does not quantify the documented backups' share of total repair. The identity of the top anti-erasure neuron varies by prompt; no one neuron is in the top 10 on more than 16% of tokens (arXiv:2402.15390 R21). That frequency measures top-ten membership, not the share of self-repair carried, and cannot determine V5's contribution claim. In arXiv:2610.04017 the compensating witnesses are generic downstream heads (untested line). In lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro, attention patterns identify candidate backup heads but do not establish their causal contribution or how much compensation they carry (r4; cannot_determine for V5).

Documented backups do not behave alike. Under an on-manifold swap, L10.h6 and L10.h1 show no coupling distinguishable from zero (arXiv:2610.02173 R17, R18), while L11.h2, L10.h2, L11.h6 and L11.h9 do (R10-R12, R14). Backups already contribute before the primaries are removed: the backup branch is at +0.567 at baseline (arXiv:2607.01940 r2). Scored alone, the backup group's NIE (0.74) exceeds the Name Movers' (0.14) (arXiv:2610.04017 r2).

Only the original measures this under ablation, and its record says the contribution depends on the ablation method, token filtering and clipping (arXiv:2402.15390 R12-R15). The other measurement audits Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-it and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with 50 matched pairs per family, under a contrastive swap. Correct-sign final-norm contributions reach 4.5% of recruitment; the largest ×1 correction is 0.6%. This is a small nonzero contribution, classified as partial; Mistral was not audited (arXiv:2610.02173 R19). It is also a normalization effect rather than a component, unlike the other named parts.

Outside the original (Pythia-160M, Llama-7B; arXiv:2402.15390 R19-R21), the neuron evidence is 'counterweight' neurons recruited by a dose-swept contrastive swap on a factual True/False task in instruct models (arXiv:2610.02173 R1-R8). The rows do not say whether these are the same neurons, or the same kind of neuron, as the anti-erasure neurons.

method_sensitivity.what: Pythia-160M head L11H2, top 2% of tokens by direct effect: the clean-to-ablated final LayerNorm scaling-factor ratio is greater than one on 90.66% of tokens under resample, 98.75% under mean and 100% under zero ablation (arXiv:2402.15390 R12-R14). The record says the LayerNorm contribution depends on the ablation method. GPT-2 small IOI, template-conditioned mean vs zero ablation: I_PB 1.080 vs 1.268, I_PE 1.830 vs 1.681, Δ(P+E) −0.136 vs −0.769 (arXiv:2608.19338 r1-r4, r9, r11). The record says direct interaction magnitudes differ between the two. A hackathon summary reports backup-head behaviour robust to the ablation distribution, without naming the distributions (lw:hhhmcWkgLwPmBuhx7 r1).

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention dose and type (swap vs deletion; on- vs off-manifold)
method_sensitivity.what: For Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct neuron L27.n13033, erased margin changes from −2.86 to −0.50 nats at ×1 and +2.93 at ×2 for true statements (R5, R7); for false statements, from −2.88 to −0.51 at ×1 and +3.22 at ×2 (R6, R8). The Qwen ×4 and Mistral endpoints are off-manifold (R3, R4); Mistral L31.n8773 is already positive on both classes at ×1. The final-norm audit covers Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-it and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with 50 matched pairs per family: correct-sign recruitment shares reach 4.5%; the largest ×1 correction is 0.6%. This small contribution under swaps need not hold for deletion (R19). The record says responses differ by model, direction and dose, joint-core swaps can recruit more than single-core ones, and responses saturate beyond full inversion.

method_sensitivity.factor: Scoring a component alone vs with downstream witnesses pinned
method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2 small IOI, counterfactual patching. The Name Movers' NIE is 0.14 scored alone and 1.16 witness-integrated (r1). The backup group's is 0.74 alone and 0.60 witness-integrated (r2). The record says the effect of witness pinning on circuit scores depends on model and metric: on GPT-2 and Llama it lowers all three reported scores, while on Qwen3 it improves the net score.

method_sensitivity.factor: Token filtering, clipping and head selection
method_sensitivity.what: The original reports LayerNorm repair at approximately 30% of clean head direct effect, using a clipped per-token ratio averaged after top-2% direct-effect filtering; this is not a measured share of total self-repair (R15). Its record says the reported fraction depends materially on filtering and clipping. Anti-erasure results use selected heads: Pythia-160M L10H11 with tokens filtered to the top 2% by final-MLP repair (R19), and Llama-7B L30H8 with top-2% head-direct-effect filtering (R20). R21 instead filters to the top 2% by head repair: no neuron appears in the per-prompt top ten on more than 16% of tokens. This frequency concerns neuron identity, not its share of total repair, which it cannot determine. The record also says self-repair varies substantially by prompt and head.

method_sensitivity.factor: Primary-set identity, replacement operator and LayerNorm freezing
method_sensitivity.what: Per the arXiv:2607.01940 record (not in rows), backup recovery varies with the identity and contamination of the primary set, the ablation replacement operator, the output geometry and the task or prompt. Freezing LayerNorm changes the AUC for detecting backups (outside rows; numbers not used here).

method_sensitivity.factor: Loss vs KL divergence on general text
method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2 Small, general text (OpenWebText): arXiv:2310.04625 Section 2.2 and Appendix C, Figure 12 report path-ablation evidence for L11H10 backing up L10H7. Controlling the L10H7-to-L11H10 path explains up to half of L10H7's indirect loss effect, with little corresponding effect on KL divergence. These general-text results are outside the extracted rows; the measured contribution depends on the output metric.

For factual True/False core-swap interventions, arXiv:2610.02173 Appendix H, Figures 17–20 compare the same identified neurons between matched base and instruct checkpoints in Llama, Gemma, Qwen and Mistral. The base checkpoints also show dose-graded recruitment, but recruitment magnitudes and restoration shares differ. Reported restoration shares are Gemma instruct 6–9%, base 11–13%; Qwen instruct 9–10%, base 22–27%; Mistral instruct 8–11%, base 24–25%. These comparisons are outside the extracted rows.
